title: Probing Ethical Framework Representations in Large Language Models: Structure, Entanglement, and Methodological Challenges
description: Probes hidden representations across 5 ethical frameworks (deontology, utilitarianism, virtue, justice, commonsense) in 6 LLMs (4B-72B params). Reveals differentiated ethical subspaces with asymmetric transfer patterns. Deontology probes partially generalize to virtue scenarios; commonsense probes fail on justice. Disagreement between deontological and utilitarian probes correlates with higher behavioral entropy.
data_available: Uses ETHICS benchmark (existing); no new dataset but novel probing methodology
recommendation_reason: March 2026. Directly probes whether LLMs distinguish normative frameworks at the representation level. Methodological contribution: shows framework entanglement and surface feature dependence. Essential for NormEval's claim about what benchmarks actually test. EPFL.

title: Does LLM Alignment Really Need Diversity? An Empirical Study of Adapting RLVR Methods for Moral Reasoning
description: First comprehensive empirical study comparing reward-maximizing and distribution-matching RLVR paradigms on MoReBench. Trains Qwen3-1.7B judge model with rubric-grounded reward pipeline. Finds moral reasoning has more concentrated high-reward distributions than math, and standard RLVR methods transfer effectively without explicit diversity mechanisms.
data_available: Uses MoReBench (existing); novel training pipeline with rubric-grounded rewards
recommendation_reason: March 2026. Microsoft Research. Uses MoReBench-Public and MoReBench-Theory subtasks. Shows how RLVR training affects moral reasoning — directly relevant to understanding what training signals benchmarks provide. Cites MoReBench extensively.

title: IslamicMMLU: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Islamic Knowledge
description: 10,013 MCQ benchmark spanning Quran (2,013), Hadith (4,000), and Fiqh/jurisprudence (4,000). Evaluates 26 LLMs. Fiqh track includes madhab bias detection task revealing school-of-thought preferences. 54-point performance gap between frontier and legacy models. HuggingFace leaderboard available.
recommendation_reason: March 2026. Largest Islamic ethics benchmark to date (10K questions). Fiqh track operationalizes Islamic legal reasoning with madhab bias detection. Addresses non-Western gap in normative benchmarks. Public data.

title: IslamicLegalBench: Evaluating LLMs Knowledge and Reasoning of Islamic Law Across 1,200 Years of Islamic Pluralist Legal Traditions
description: First benchmark evaluating LLMs across 7 schools of Islamic jurisprudence. 718 instances covering 13 tasks from 38 foundational legal texts spanning 1,200 years. Tasks range from basic recall to analogical application (qiyas) and cross-school synthesis. Best model: 68% correctness with 21% hallucination. 20% public dev set.
recommendation_reason: February 2026. Operationalizes Islamic legal reasoning (qiyas = analogical reasoning similar to deontological case analysis). Tests across 7 jurisprudential schools — strong normative pluralism. Submitted to AI & Law.

title: Are LLMs Complicated Ethical Dilemma Analyzers?
description: 196 real-world ethical dilemmas from Georgia CTSA repository and Online Ethics Center. Each case segmented into 5 components: Introduction, Key Factors, Historical Theoretical Perspectives, Resolution Strategies, Key Takeaways. Expert opinions + non-expert human responses. Evaluates GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Deepseek-V3, Gemini-1.5-Flash.
data_available: Dataset from Georgia CTSA repository; research ethics cases
recommendation_reason: May 2025. Novel approach using real academic research ethics cases with expert annotations. 196 dilemmas with structured components including Historical Theoretical Perspectives — tests whether LLMs can engage with normative theory. Ecological validity.

title: MFTCXplain: A Multilingual Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating the Moral Reasoning of LLMs through Multi-hop Hate Speech Explanation
description: 3,000 tweets across Portuguese, Italian, Persian, English annotated with binary hate speech labels, moral categories (MFT), and text span-level rationales. Multi-hop explanation task. LLMs achieve F1 up to 0.836 on hate speech detection but <0.35 on moral sentiment prediction.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Trager-MFTCXplain.md. Uses MFT (descriptive), not normative ethics frameworks. Low relevance to normative ethics benchmarking.

title: The Staircase of Ethics: Probing LLM Value Priorities through Multi-Step Induction to Complex Moral Dilemmas
description: Multi-step Moral Dilemmas (MMDs): 3,302 five-stage dilemmas. Progressive escalation forces LLMs to recalibrate moral judgments. 9 LLMs evaluated. Value preferences shift significantly as dilemmas progress. Care often prioritized but superseded by fairness contextually.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault (2 entries: 2025-Wu and 2025-Unknown). Already identified by vault mining Agent 1C. Uses Schwartz value theory rather than normative ethics frameworks directly.

title: The Moral Consistency Pipeline: Continuous Ethical Evaluation for Large Language Models
description: MoCoP: Dataset-free, closed-loop framework for continuously evaluating moral stability. Three layers: lexical integrity, semantic risk estimation, reasoning-based judgment. Evaluates GPT-4-Turbo and DeepSeek. Strong inverse correlation between ethical and toxicity dimensions (r=-0.81).
data_available: Framework is dataset-free (generative); no static benchmark
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Jamshidi-MoCoP.md. Evaluation methodology rather than normative ethics benchmark. Does not test specific normative traditions.

title: Understanding Moral Reasoning Trajectories in Large Language Models: Toward Probing-Based Explainability
description: Introduces moral reasoning trajectories — sequences of ethical framework invocations across reasoning steps. 55-57% of consecutive steps involve framework switches; only 16-18% remain framework-consistent. Unstable trajectories 1.29x more susceptible to persuasive attacks. Proposes Moral Representation Consistency (MRC) metric.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2026-Unknown-Understanding Moral Reasoning Trajectories.md. Methodology paper, not new benchmark. But important: shows LLMs switch between frameworks 55-57% of the time — key finding for NormEval's argument.

title: Values in the Wild: Discovering and Analyzing Values in Real-World Language Model Interactions
description: Analyzes 700K anonymized Claude.ai conversations. Discovers 3,307 AI values via bottom-up taxonomy. Tests prosocial value support and resistance to moral nihilism. 3% strong resistance cases involve ethical boundary enforcement.
data_available: Methodology described but raw data not public (privacy)
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Huang-Values in the Wild.md. Value taxonomy study, not normative ethics benchmark. No evaluation dataset.

title: IslamTrust: A Benchmark for LLMs Alignment with Islamic Values
description: 406 MCQ questions across 6 domains in Arabic and English. Evaluates LLM alignment with consensus-based Islamic ethical principles across Sunni schools. Best model: 66.5% overall. Models struggle with Islamic values due to limited training representation.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault (2 entries: 2025-Lahmar). Already in feature matrix or vault mining. Relevant for non-Western coverage but already tracked.

title: A Roadmap for Evaluating Moral Competence in Large Language Models
description: Nature paper calling for shift from moral performance to moral competence evaluation. Three challenges: facsimile problem, moral multidimensionality, moral pluralism. Proposes adversarial and confirmatory evaluation methods. Advocates testing with unseen scenarios, context sensitivity, and framework adaptation.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2026-Gabriel-roadmap evaluating moral competence.md. Position paper in Nature (very high impact). No new benchmark but essential theoretical framing for NormEval. Already cited.

title: Mapping Moral Reasoning in LLMs: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Safety Principle Conflicts
description: Analyzes how open-weight LLMs resolve conflicts between competing safety principles (public welfare, institutional transparency, individual rights). Each response encoded into 11-dimensional normative profile using semantic similarity to canonical ethical theories and dictionary-based moral cues.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Mahajan-Mapping Moral Reasoning in LLMs.md. Analysis methodology, not new benchmark dataset.

title: ProMoral-Bench: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Moral Reasoning and Safety in LLMs
description: Unified benchmark evaluating 11 prompting paradigms across 4 LLM families (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet-4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek-V3). Uses ETHICS, Scruples, WildJailbreak, and novel ETHICS-Contrast robustness test. Proposes Unified Moral Safety Score (UMSS). Compact exemplar-guided scaffolds outperform complex multi-stage reasoning.
data_available: Uses existing datasets + novel ETHICS-Contrast; likely GitHub
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2026-Thomas-ProMoral-Bench.md. Already in feature matrix (#37). Evaluation of prompting strategies rather than new normative benchmark.

title: Discerning What Matters: A Multi-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Competence in LLMs
description: Assesses moral competence across 5 dimensions: identifying morally relevant features, weighting importance, assigning moral reasons, synthesizing coherent judgments. Novel multi-dimensional methodology beyond simple accuracy.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Kilov-Discerning What Matters.md. Methodology for moral competence assessment, not normative ethics benchmark.

title: How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?
description: Review of 210 safety benchmarks mapping challenges. Argues safety benchmarks are normative rather than descriptive, assessing potential for harm rather than task proficiency. Identifies technical, epistemic, and sociotechnical shortcomings.
recommendation_reason: January 2026. Meta-analysis of 210 safety benchmarks. Relevant to NormEval's framing (safety benchmarks as normative instruments) but does not introduce a new normative ethics benchmark. Useful as supporting citation.

title: Mind the Gap! Pathways Towards Unifying AI Safety and Ethics Research
description: Argues for integrating technical safety work with normative ethics via shared benchmarks, cross-institutional venues, and mixed-method methodologies.
recommendation_reason: December 2025. Position paper calling for safety-ethics integration. No benchmark data but directly supports NormEval paper's argument about the safety-ethics gap in benchmarks.

title: Legal Alignment for Safe and Ethical AI
description: Proposes legal alignment to augment Constitutional AI. Formal and textualist tools address ambiguity in normative alignment specifications. Argues legal rules provide substantive content for safety specifications.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2026-Kolt-Legal Alignment for Safe and Ethical AI.md. Theory paper connecting legal reasoning to AI alignment. No benchmark.

title: C-VARC: A Large-Scale Chinese Value Rule Corpus for Value Alignment of Large Language Models
description: 250K+ value rules in hierarchical framework: 3 dimensions, 12 core values, 50 derived values. Grounded in Chinese cultural values (Confucian). 400K rule-based moral dilemma scenarios. LLMs preferred CVC options in 70.5%+ of cases; 87.5% human alignment.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Wu-CVC.md. Already identified by vault mining Agent 1C as INCLUDE candidate. Strong Confucian ethics coverage.

title: Mapping Moral Reasoning Circuits: A Mechanistic Analysis of Ethical Decision-Making in Large Language Models
description: Mechanistic interpretability study of how LLMs encode moral reasoning across 6 moral dimensions: care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity, liberty.
recommendation_reason: Already in vault as 2025-Schacht-Mapping Moral Reasoning Circuits.md. MFT-based (descriptive), not normative ethics.

title: RAIL in the Wild: Operationalizing Responsible AI Evaluation Using Anthropic's Value Dataset
description: Operationalizes responsible AI evaluation using the Values in the Wild dataset from Anthropic. Builds evaluation framework from the 3,307 discovered AI values.
data_available: Uses Anthropic's Values in the Wild data
recommendation_reason: May 2025. Operationalizes Anthropic's value taxonomy for evaluation. Not a normative ethics benchmark per se, but relevant to the Constitutional AI evaluation landscape.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Islamic Ethics: Towards Pluralist Ethical Benchmarking for AI
description: Theoretical paper proposing pluralist ethical benchmarking that incorporates Islamic ethics (Trusteeship Ethics). Argues current AI ethics benchmarks are Western-centric.
recommendation_reason: 2023. Foundational theory paper for Islamic AI ethics benchmarking. No dataset but provides philosophical grounding for non-Western benchmark development. Good background citation.

title: Islamic Ethics and AI: An Evaluation of Existing Approaches to AI using Trusteeship Ethics
description: Evaluates existing AI ethics approaches through Islamic Trusteeship Ethics (Amanah) framework. Proposes alternative ethical lens for AI governance.
recommendation_reason: 2025. Theoretical framework applying Islamic Trusteeship Ethics to AI. No benchmark but relevant context for Islamic ethics evaluation gap.

title: Dharma Setu: Bridging Ancient Buddhist Wisdom and Modern AI Through Multimodal Integration
description: Framework exploring intersections between Buddhist wisdom traditions and AI. Draws on 10 billion tokens from Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
recommendation_reason: 2025. First attempt to bridge Buddhist ethics and AI with substantial corpus (10B tokens). Not a benchmark but could inform Buddhist ethics evaluation development. Notable gap: no dedicated Buddhist ethics LLM benchmark exists.

title: Assessing Large Language Models on Islamic Legal Reasoning: Evidence from Inheritance Law Evaluation
description: Evaluates LLMs on Islamic inheritance law (Mawarith). Tests mathematical computation and legal reasoning required for inheritance distribution across Islamic jurisprudence.
data_available: ArabicNLP published; specific to inheritance law
recommendation_reason: 2025. Narrow-domain Islamic legal reasoning (inheritance only). Mathematical component dominates. Less relevant to broad normative ethics benchmarking but part of growing Islamic AI evaluation ecosystem.
